header.label: Construction planning
header.title: Open Planner Studio
header.desc: Open-source construction planning with Gantt charts, critical path, resources and levelling, baselines and progress — and native IFC 4.3 as the file format. Shared resource libraries show how heavily a crew or machine is committed across all your projects, and a built-in MCP server lets an AI assistant read and edit your schedule. On your desktop and straight in the browser.

download.title: Download v2026.8.0
download.browserNote: Rather not install anything? Open Planner Studio also runs fully in your browser — including opening and saving files.

ai.title: AI assistant via MCP
ai.desc: An MCP server is built into the app, so an AI client such as Claude Code can read and edit your schedule directly. Switch it on in the AI tab, with a pause button, read-only mode and automatic backups.

gantt.title: Gantt charts
gantt.desc: Interactive HTML5 Canvas Gantt with drag and drop, zoom and timeline navigation. Drag a whole selection vertically, collapse non-working days out of the timeline and select with Ctrl+click. Week numbers in the header.

cpm.title: Critical path (CPM)
cpm.desc: Automatic critical path calculation with float, near-critical work, multiple critical paths and deadline analysis.

wbs.title: WBS & table view
wbs.desc: Hierarchical task structure with collapsible chapters. The table edits like a spreadsheet: type in the cell, grab several rows at once and drag rows around.

ifc.title: Native IFC 4.3
ifc.desc: Your schedule is an IFC file (buildingSMART standard). With a built-in IFC code editor to generate and apply.

resources.title: Resources & levelling
resources.desc: Labour, equipment and subcontractors with a histogram and automatic levelling of overallocation. Move assignments while keeping units and curve.

library.title: Resource libraries
library.desc: Share one resource pool across several projects. The library is the source, the project shows what it actually uses, and deviations are flagged so you can resolve them. The occupancy overview adds up every open project — as a table and as a histogram — and marks the days where the committed load exceeds the available capacity.

baselines.title: Baselines & progress
baselines.desc: Capture multiple baselines and record progress with a status date, actual start and a cleaned-up progress line.

calendars.title: Calendars & hourly planning
calendars.desc: Construction-specific calendars: public holidays, building recess, frost delay, inspection moments and phasing. Plan down to the hour.

browser.title: Desktop and browser
browser.desc: Runs natively on Windows, macOS and Linux, but also fully in the browser — including open, save, auto-save and crash recovery.

exchange.title: Exchange
exchange.desc: Import and export IFC, CSV, MS Project (.xml) and Primavera P6 (.xml) — no intermediate steps or conversion tools.

bim4d.title: 4D BIM-ready
bim4d.desc: Link planning tasks to elements from your IFC building model for 4D visualisation of the construction sequence.

reporting.title: Reporting & printing
reporting.desc: Live print preview in the ribbon and export to a real high-resolution PDF (±220 DPI). Configurable font size, a header that repeats on every page and a timeline that may span several pages. Your settings are remembered.

docs.title: Manual inside the app
docs.desc: Press F1 for an offline manual, available in all fourteen languages: quick start, practical guides — including resource libraries and connecting an AI assistant — and fifteen reference pages, plus three sample projects to practise on.

shortcuts.title: Shortcuts & context menus
shortcuts.desc: Full overview via Ctrl+/ and rich right-click menus on the task row, Gantt bar, canvas and band header. Per-task notes with a tickable checklist.

multilingual.title: 14 languages
multilingual.desc: Nederlands, English, Français, Deutsch, Español, Italiano, Português, Polski, Türkçe, 中文, 日本語, 한국어 and RTL support for العربية and فارسی.

ribbon.title: Ribbon toolbar
ribbon.desc: Familiar Office-style ribbon with tabs: Home, Planning, View, Settings, Table, IFC and Report.

tauri.title: Tauri 2
tauri.desc: Native desktop app with a Rust backend for Windows, macOS and Linux.

react.title: React 19 + TypeScript
react.desc: Component-based UI with Zustand + Immer for state management.

canvas.title: HTML5 Canvas 2D
canvas.desc: Gantt rendering. TailwindCSS 4 for styling, Vite 7 as the build.

whatsnew.label: New in v2026.8.0 · testers wanted
whatsnew.title: See at a glance whether the same crew is booked twice
whatsnew.desc: A resource library is one shared pool across several projects. New is the occupancy overview: per library item you see — as a table and as a histogram — how much of it is already committed across all your open projects together. One crew or machine scheduled on two projects at once becomes visible instead of implicit; a single project cannot show that by definition.
whatsnew.testers: We are looking for testers: work planners, schedulers, project leads and BIM coordinators. Try Open Planner Studio right in your browser and tell us what you think — your feedback helps shape where it goes.
whatsnew.list:
• Occupancy overview — the committed load per crew, machine or subcontractor across all your open projects, with capacity overruns flagged.
  • Relations on milestones and summary tasks — dragging a relation from a milestone works again, relations that cannot have any effect are marked instead of silently ignored, and an imported file keeps everything it came with.
  • Task type inherited from the parent task — both for a task you add yourself and for one the AI assistant creates.
  • Sample projects with resources — the bundled examples now show resource planning and the occupancy overview with real data.

import.q: Can I open files from Microsoft Project or Primavera P6?
import.a: Yes. Open Planner Studio imports and exports MS Project (.xml) and Primavera P6 (.xml) directly, with no intermediate step or conversion tool. IFC and CSV are supported as well.

browser.q: Do I have to install anything?
browser.a: No. The full application runs in the browser, including opening and saving files, auto-save and crash recovery. In Chromium browsers (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi) Ctrl+S saves back over the same file, just like on the desktop; Firefox and Safari fall back to the file picker. If you do want to install, there are builds for Windows, macOS and Linux.

formaat.q: What file format is my schedule saved in?
formaat.a: IFC 4.3, the open buildingSMART standard. Your schedule *is* an IFC file — there is no proprietary, closed format. That keeps your data readable outside this application, and lets you link schedule tasks to elements in an IFC building model for 4D.

ai.q: What exactly can an AI assistant do with my schedule?
ai.a: Since v2026.7.13 the app ships a built-in MCP server. An AI client such as Claude Code can read your schedule through it — project overview, tasks, critical path, resources, histogram, calendars and baselines — and edit it too. You switch the bridge on in the AI tab and stay in control: there is a pause button, a read-only mode, automatic backups and an activity panel listing every call the assistant made.

prijs.q: What does Open Planner Studio cost?
prijs.a: Nothing. The application is free and open source under the LGPL-3.0 licence. No subscription, no per-seat licence fees.

platforms.q: Which systems does it run on?
platforms.a: Windows (.exe), macOS (universal .dmg, both Intel and Apple Silicon) and Linux (.deb, .rpm, AppImage and snap). Plus fully in the browser.

bouwpraktijk.a: Yes. You set up construction-specific calendars with public holidays, building recess, frost delay, inspection moments and phasing, and you can plan down to hour level. The interface is available in fourteen languages.

analyse.q: Can I see which tasks drive the end date?
analyse.a: Yes. The critical path is calculated automatically, with float, near-critical work, multiple critical paths and deadline analysis. Resources get a histogram with automatic levelling of overallocation, and multiple baselines let you track deviations from the original plan.
